newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Toyota Safrica to cut minibus prices 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Toyota Safrica to cut minibus prices 20 pct.

text.p: Toyota South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it was slashing the price of its minibus vehicles, used mainly by taxi operators, by 20 percent.

Johan van Zyl, managing director of vehicle marketing, said the move reflected growing awareness of an "affordability crisis" that was adversely affecting this sector of the vehicle industry which provides transport for about 13 million people.

He said in a statement that sales of the minibus had also dropped sharply from the boom years 1988-1990 when some 27,441 minibuses were sold. This figure was higher than the total sales in the past six years, he said.
Agreement on the price cuts had been reached with Japan's Toyota Motor Corporation, which last year bought a 28.7 percent stake in the South African firm, and Toyota's dealers.
"We have negotiated a package which will see all three parties contribute to a reduction of 20 percent in the price of our taxi (minibus) models," van Zyl said.
Toyota South Africa, which van Zyl said controlled 73.4 percent of the country's taxi market in 1996, also said it would be rationalising its minibus production range by discontinuing three models.
However, the three remaining models -- the Hi-Ace Super 16, Super T and Hi-Ace panel van -- would continue being manufactured in South Africa well beyond the year 2000, van Zyl said.
